page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.4xlarge is an extreme memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz across 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration provides dedicated resource allocation with 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a large 54 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators like AES and VAES.

The primary architectural distinction of the x2iedn.4xlarge is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio. It provides 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage includes an integrated local 475 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, bundled alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance contains no GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier compute and memory throughput relative to the broader cloud market. The platform achieved 1,891.88 single-core and 15,459.07 multi-core points in stress-ng, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 1,624.0 and multi-core score of 9,759.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 98.18 GB/sec read and 53.57 GB/sec write for large uncached blocks, supporting 15.66 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and a PassMark database score of 7,637.85. Medium model LLM prompt processing falls in the bottom 25% (31.41 tokens/sec), reflecting the limitations of CPU-bound inference.

Cost efficiency is centered around applications with exceptional memory footprint requirements relative to compute. The 32:1 RAM-to-vCPU density prevents the need to over-provision compute cores solely to satisfy memory limits. The instance is suited for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching layers, and high-footprint enterprise ERP applications like SAP HANA.
